title: Streaming Tool Integration Test Harness Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical playbook for building a repeatable test harness and scenario matrix for streaming-hosted API integrations that exercise tool-calling, structured output frames, partial/resumable responses, and client SDK ergonomics. The intent is pragmatic: enable engineers and QA to reproduce edge cases seen in customer integrations and validate SDK behavior under realistic network and model conditions.

Background and motivation:
- We keep seeing flaky integrations where clients lose tool responses mid-stream, replay incorrectly, or mis-handle partial structured frames.
- Existing unit tests catch parsing logic but not the interplay of network interruptions, backpressure, and client-side snapshot/reconciliation.
- This doc proposes a light-weight harness pattern that teams can adopt to run deterministic scenarios locally and in CI.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
1) Reproducible scenarios that capture: tool-call retries, partial JSON frames, interleaved text+tool payloads, and deliberate latency spikes.
2) Deterministic asserts for client SDKs: idempotent tool application, resume semantics (checkpointing), and schema validation against expected structured outputs.
3) Easy-to-run harness: single command to run a scenario locally, and a shim to run in CI with varied network profiles.
4) Telemetry hooks: each scenario emits structured event logs compatible with Console traces (route, model, client sdk version, scenario id).

Scope (what this playbook covers):
- Streaming responses from Hosted API that may contain: free-text tokens, structured "action" frames, tool-call request/response frames, and final commit frames.
- Client-driven resumes where the client replays a cached transcript or requests a continuation token.
- SDK behaviors: parsing incremental frames, queuing tool invocations to the app, deduplication of tool results, and recovery after partial disconnects.
- Not in scope: model evaluation of semantic correctness beyond framing/structure, deep fuzzing of proto tokenization.

Core components of the harness:
1) Scenario driver (python/ts): describes timeline of server events (send X tokens, emit tool-call frame, pause, inject error, re-send tool result). Scenario format is YAML/JSON.
2) Mock Hosted proxy: a tiny server that speaks the streaming protocol and can be scripted by the scenario driver (supports chunked transfer, deliberate socket close, HTTP2 RESET simulation).
3) SDK test adapter: small test harness that wraps the real SDK bindings and exposes hooks for injecting network constraints and inspecting internal reconcilers/checkpoints.
4) App stub: a lightweight process that consumes tool-call requests the SDK would surface and replies with scripted tool outputs (to test idempotency and ordering).
5) Assert library: reusable assertions for common invariants (no duplicate tool application, final JSON parseable by schema X, client resumes from last committed action).
6) Telemetry forwarder: writes scenario events to a standard trace format used by Console, with scenario and run IDs.

Canonical scenarios (start minimal, grow coverage):
A. Partial Frame, then Resume
- Server: stream partial JSON action frame (truncated mid-field), close socket.
- Client expectation: SDK emits a parse-error event for incomplete frame, persists checkpoint at last committed frame, on re-open it requests continuation; when server re-sends frame completion, SDK emits single tool-call to app stub.
- Assert: single tool invocation; final structured output matches schema.

B. Tool Result Duplication under Retry
- Server: emits tool-call request frame; app stub delays response; client-side retry logic causes duplicate request to be delivered to app stub; app stub returns same result both times.
- Client expectation: SDK deduplicates based on request id and surfaces only one result to application layer.
- Assert: app stub sees 2 requests but app layer only receives 1 application-level invocation.

C. Interleaved Text + Tool Flow with Backpressure
- Server: stream text tokens, inject a large tool-call frame which blocks token stream until tool result arrives. Simulate slow downstream consumer to trigger client SDK backpressure behavior.
- Client expectation: SDK should keep token streaming minimally buffered, maintain low latency for each token, and not drop tool frames.
- Metrics: measure tokens-in-flight, latency tail (95/99th) for token delivery, memory usage.

D. Alternate-model-fallback while Streaming
- Server: mid-stream injects a fallback hint to use a cheaper model variant; server then streams a compacted partial output format.
- Client expectation: SDK applies fallback policy and can request model-mapped parsing rules; no duplicative tool-calls or lost frames.

E. Offline Replay + Snapshot Reconciliation
- Scenario: client loses connectivity after seeing tool-call result but before acknowledging. Client replays transcript from disk to reconcile which actions were committed.
- Expectation: SDK reconciler rehydrates state, identifies already-applied tool results via stable ids, and avoids re-executing actions.

Test data and schemas:
- Provide canonical JSON schemas for action frames (action.request, action.response, action.commit), and example transcripts. Keep versions in a small fixtures directory so CI can pin schema versions when running tests.

Acceptance criteria (per scenario):
- Pass/fail determinism: assertion pass rate > 99% across 50 runs in CI under stable environment.
- Instrumented traces include scenario id, sdk version, route, model, and per-frame timings.
- New SDK regressions should include a reproducible scenario and a minimal failing transcript attached to the failing job.

CI integration strategy:
- Unit vs integration: unit tests remain fast and isolated. These harness scenarios are integration-level and run nightly and as part of release gates.
- Parallelization: scenario instances are isolated by scenario-id and allocated ephemeral ports; tests run in parallel on CI workers.
- Flakiness handling: failures automatically re-run up to 2 times; persistent failures create a ticket and upload trace bundle.

Developer quickstart (local):
1) git clone github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk && cd hosted-sdk/tests/harness
2) pip install -r requirements.txt or npm i
3) python harness/runner.py --scenario partial-frame-resume --sdk ./dist/my-sdk.js --port 8089
4) harness starts proxy, app stub, and collects traces in ./runs/<timestamp>. Run replay: python harness/inspect.py <run-id>

Telemetry and observability hooks we need:
- For each scenario event: scenario_id, step_id, frame_id, timestamp, action_id, sdk_version, client_host, route, model_id, bytes_sent, bytes_received, error_code, stack (if error).
- Console-side: map scenario runs to per-route dashboards so product engineers can quickly see real-world analogs.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How much of this belongs in product-owned test infra vs SDK team ownership? Proposal: product defines scenarios and shared harness; SDKs provide adapters and CI jobs.
- Determinism vs realism: full network fuzzing increases realism but reduces determinism. Start with scripted profiles; add fuzz runs in canary pipeline.
- Persistent id scheme for tool-call dedupe: use a combination of request-id + client-instance-id; need to standardize across SDKs.

Next steps (practical roadmap):
- Week 0–1: land minimal harness: scenario driver, mock proxy, one SDK adapter for Node and Python.
- Week 2–3: add 6 canonical scenarios (A–F) and integrate into nightly CI.
- Week 4: add telemetry forwarder and Console trace mapping for scenario runs.
- Week 5+: roll out to other SDKs and refine based on early failures.

Appendix: quick checklist for creating new scenarios
- Describe clear invariants and expected side-effects (e.g., "only one app-layer invocation").
- Provide minimal transcript fixture that reproduces the behavior.
- Tag scenario with product area, e.g., "tools", "resumption", "schema".
- Attach suggested telemetry fields to emit.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft. Feedback requested on the scenario set (what else should we include?) and proposed ownership split. If you want to try it locally ping #hosted-sdk-harness on Slack with your OS and preferred SDK (node/python/rust).
